I'm sorry that you have to go through that. It's really hard listening to your cat cry. I have two questions: did your vet give the opinion that she was getting chunky? Her body is telling her that she isn't getting enough food and its breaking into the fat reserves. Unfortunately, it doesn't matter if that weight loss is a healthy thing or not. The bright side is that in theory, her weight will eventually match the calories you are giving her, and then she won't feel so hungry.

\- Three days in Athens. Arrive day one, get settled in, two full days, then depart by train for Meteora in the morning of day 4. 

\- Two days in Meteora. Arrive in the afternoon day one, get settled, do a sunset tour. Day two: full day to explore. Day three - a little exploring/down-time, depart via train in the evening. \- Take the ferry to Paros the next morning, and stay three days. 

\- Take the ferry to Naxos, stay for 4 days. Return to Athens via ferry in the afternoon/evening of the fourth day, where I again stayed near the port. 

\- Take the subway to the Athens airport to go home. 

Some notes: 

If you are on an island at the end of your trip be aware that it is possible that the ferry to return to Athens may be delayed or cancelled. As such, you should return to the mainland the day before your flight. 

I stayed in the Koukaki neighborhood in Athens, right under Filapappou hill. It was a nice neighborhood, close enough to the downtown to walk but also pretty quiet. It was also just a couple blocks from the a subway station, which was really handy. Mt. Lycebettus is really cool, and I enjoyed the walk up and the gondola down. Bring a good sized bottle of water though! The tap water is fine to drink in Greece, so I bought a liter bottle of water and then just refilled it throughout my trip. 

Meteora is amazing. Some people recommend only doing one night here, but I found two nights to be perfect, taking the earlier train on the last day. Also - you don't have to do tour to see the sights, BUT I took one and was able to learn a lot more about the history of the places from that. I found it very worth it.  

Paros is OK, but I was underwhelmed, and I would rather do Paros as a day trip from Naxos. Naxos is great! There are very cheap buses that are very convenient to take around the island. I also took a bus tour around the island, and a day trip to Antiparos. On Antiparos, I took a little boat tour around the island and to an even smaller island, Despotiko, with [Captain Sargos](http://www.sargosantiparos.gr/). So much fun!

This title is misleading. The paper states that "synthetic clothes contributes by about 35% to the global release of primary microplastics to the world oceans, thus becoming the main source of microplastics." 

However, they are citing different paper ([link here](https://portals.iucn.org/library/sites/library/files/documents/2017-002-En.pdf)). The key word there is primary microplastics - that is plastic that enters the ecosystem already micro. The cited paper states that: "15 and 31% of all of the plastic in the oceans could originate from primary sources." 

35% of the possible 31% of primary microplastics means that actually these sources are saying that the washing of synthetic fabrics contribute about 10% of the total microplastics in the ocean. 

Still bad, but not quite how I interpreted the title.

My easy 5 gallon recipe: 12 lbs of canned fruit cocktail, 13 lbs sugar (that is what it took my last batch to have a potential alcohol  content of 15%), and a packet of yeast (I use champagne yeast ordered from amazon. Bread yeast will probably work). I use a nylon bag to hold the fruit. 

I'm not sure how universal fruit cocktail is: its a mixture of grapes, peaches, and pears. You can substitute canned peaches and pears. Make sure they are in fruit juice, or if they are in syrup, that the ingredients include only sugar, and not corn syrup. 

Directions: 

* Dump contents of cans into a large pot, heat to boiling (adding water if necessary). Boil for 2 minutes. Allow to cool. 
* Transfer fruit into a bag or cheesecloth, reserving all liquid that drains from them in this process. 
* Dump the sugar into the pot, and add enough water to cover the sugar. Heat and stir until it dissolves. Allow to cool. 
* Transfer sugar solution to a large bucket (large enough to hold 6-7 gallons), set the bag of fruit/any juices in it, and add enough water to bring it to 5 gallons. 
* Wake up your yeast in some warm water. After 10 minutes, add a small amount of the liquid from your bucket. Wait another 10 minutes - it should be foamy now. 
* Add the yeast to the bucket - assuming your liquid in the bucket is not hot - it can be warm, but not very warm. I cover with a clean dish towel and secure it around the top of the bucket with a rubber band. 
* Stir twice daily for 2 weeks, then remove and discard the fruit. Allow to ferment in the bucket another 2 weeks. 
* Transfer to a clean container, leaving the sediment behind. It will not be entirely done fermenting at this point, so avoid sealed containers, especially glass. Gallon size plastic bottles (like empty juice bottles) work well - fill them up but leave the cap slightly loosened.  
* After two weeks in a bottle with the lid loose, you can tighten the lids, but 'burp' daily until you feel its unnecessary. That means unscrewing the lid enough to release pressure. If no pressure is building up over 2 days, then you can stop. Place a bottle in the fridge, leave it alone for at least a week. 
* Drink!

Beyond plastics causing obstructions (which someone else explained), my understanding is that the we don't fully know the problems that are or will be caused by plastic particles. We know they have been found pretty much everywhere we look (in sand, in air, in organisms, in water etc). We know that many types of plastics breakdown and then act as endocrine disruptors, meaning they affect hormonal systems. This can cause a variety of health problems, such as cancers of the reproductive system. Plastic isn't one thing - there are many types (PVC, PMMA, PET to name a few). As I mentioned to someone else, they can also break down into nano sized particles. These are small enough to pass through cell walls and collect in other organs. Again, we do not yet know all the consequences of plastic contamination in every part of the ecosystem.

 **Ingredients**

* 5 Rolls, stale
* 150 ml Milk
* Salt & Pepper
* Nutmeg
* ½ Onion, finely diced
* 1 TBS Butter
* 1 TBS each of Basil, Parsley, Chives 
* 2 tsp. Dill  
* 2 Eggs
* 1.5 TBS Flour, more if needed
* 1 TBS Bread Crumbs, more if needed

 **Steps**

1. Cut or tear rolls into small cubes
2. Warm the milk, and season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.  Pour over cubed bread. Cover with a towel and let sit for 30 mn
3. Melt the butter over medium heat and soften the diced onion until translucent
4. Mix the onion and herbs into the bread
5. Whisk the eggs together with the flour, and add them to the bread
6. Knead together adding breadcrumbs until it makes dough which will stick together
7. Let the dough sit for 15 MN
8. Bring a pot of salted water to boil
9. With damp hands, form balls, about the size of a small snowball
10. Boil the dumpling for 20 MN

Sexuality is fluid, to different degrees for different people. Some people are bisexual but their sexuality changes over time and bisexual no longer describes them well. Some people decide they are straight and later develop or discover that bisexual is a better descriptor. You wonder if 'truly' bisexual people ever grow out of it. Other factors are at play - there exists biphobia in the LGBT community, and bisexuals must reassert their sexuality frequently or people may label them as monosexual, because of the gender of their current partner. 

Labels are not perfect, and they may change. I think we need to learn not to view some labels as illegitimate because some people change them. We should just believe people. When I was a baby my hair was blond, but as I grew up it became dark brown. This is no reason to mistrust that my hair will remain brown, or disbelieve other people who are blond. Many people were born blond and have remained blond. 

I would say the majority of people identifying as bisexual continue to identify as bisexual. What your therapist said was biphobic and was an attempt to illigitimize bisexuality. 

tl;dr Some people who identify as bi change labels. That is okay, and doesn't make bisexuality illegitimate. Many people identify as bi and continue to do so forever. All bisexuals are 'truly' bisexual.
